span.label: method
span.quote: Drawing on the synthesized literature, an integrative appraisal matrix was developed.

span.label: critical appraisal of evidence in medical education
span.quote: This review confirms that critical appraisal in medical education must extend beyond rigid methodological hierarchies.

span.label: systematic-review
span.quote: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines (7).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Educational interventions sit inside complex social systems, which blocks causal attribution and so makes biomedical evidence hierarchies inapplicable.
span.quote: Educational interventions are often embedded within complex social systems, making causal attribution difficult and limiting the applicability of traditional evidence hierarchies (6).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Absent an explicit theoretical frame, a study stays descriptive, which drains its explanatory power and stops findings accumulating across the field.
span.quote: Without theoretical grounding, studies often remain descriptive, limiting their explanatory power and their capacity to contribute cumulatively to the field.

span.label: Restricted to English-language publications and excluded grey literature.
span.quote: This review was limited to English-language publications and did not include grey literature.

span.label: The narrative synthesis approach may introduce interpretive bias.
span.quote: Narrative synthesis may also introduce interpretive bias.

span.label: The review's whole object is the import of evidence-based medicine's appraisal principles and evidence hierarchies into medical education, an import it judges conceptually and methodologically problematic and then reworks into an education-specific matrix.
span.quote: While the principles of evidence-based medicine have substantially shaped clinical decision-making, their direct transfer to educational contexts has proven conceptually methodologically challenging.

span.label: editorials without methodological content and purely clinical studies excluded before appraisal
span.note: eliminates: an appraisal of evidence quality carried out on documents that make no methodological claim
span.quote: Editorials without methodological content and purely clinical studies were excluded.

span.label: Of 1,246 records retrieved by the database search, 84 studies met the inclusion criteria.
span.quote: The database search yielded 1,246 records. After removal of duplicates and screening, 84 studies met the inclusion criteria.

span.label: Evidence in medical education research falls into four types: quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, and design-based research.
span.quote: categorized into quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, and design-based research.

span.label: Biomedical evidence hierarchies imported into medical education failed to capture educational relevance and contextual complexity.
span.quote: Traditional biomedical hierarchies were insufficient to capture educational relevance and contextual complexity.

span.label: BEME, MERSQI, CASP and realist review frameworks were the appraisal tools most often cited, but they were applied inconsistently across the included studies.
span.quote: Appraisal tools such as BEME, MERSQI, CASP, and realist review frameworks were commonly cited, yet inconsistently applied.

span.label: Randomised controlled trials were frequently impractical or educationally reductive in education settings, while qualitative and theory-driven studies were undervalued despite being methodologically rigorous.
span.quote: Randomized controlled trials, while methodologically robust, were often impractical or educationally reductive (6,12). Conversely, qualitative and theorydriven research, despite methodological rigor, was frequently undervalued (19,25).

span.label: Theory is underused throughout the reviewed medical education research and appraisal literature.
span.quote: A recurring theme across the reviewed literature is the underutilization of theory in medical education research and appraisal.

span.label: The review's product is an integrative appraisal matrix built from the synthesised literature rather than from a single quality score.
span.quote: Drawing on the synthesized literature, an integrative appraisal matrix was developed.

span.label: The proposed matrix scores studies on six domains - relevance, methodological rigor, theoretical grounding, outcomes meaningfulness, context, and impact - instead of reducing quality to one number.
span.quote: By integrating domains such as relevance, methodological rigor, theoretical grounding, outcomes meaningfulness, context, and impact, the matrix moves beyond reductionist quality scoring systems.

span.label: transferability (as the appraisal standard replacing generalizability)
span.term: transferability (as the appraisal standard replacing generalizability)
span.quote: generalizability, as traditionally conceived in biomedical research, is rarely attainable in medical education. Instead, the concept of transferability offers a more appropriate standard.

span.label: context (as an appraisal domain, not a nuisance variable)
span.term: context (as an appraisal domain, not a nuisance variable)
span.quote: context is not a methodological nuisance to be controlled, but a central determinant of

span.quote: The database search yielded 1,246 records.

span.quote: The database search yielded 1,246 records. After removal of duplicates and screening, 84 studies met the inclusion criteria.

span.label: 2000 and 2024 — publication window for eligible studies in the four databases searched
span.quote: Searches were performed in MEDLINE (PubMed), ERIC, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2000 and 2024.
